newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka troops find big food stocks in rebel area.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka troops find big food stocks in rebel area.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops who launched a fresh offensive against Tamil Tiger separatists last month have recovered huge stockpiles of food in newly-captured rebel areas, the Defence ministry said on Sunday.

The announcement followed accusations by the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels that the government had killed Tamil civilians and started a "food siege" in the area under attack, displacing many Tamils and cutting off supplies.

The Defence Ministry statement said that troops had found thousands of tonnes of food in Nedunkeni, apparently left behind by the LTTE rebels when government troops captured the northern town after fierce fighting.
It said the stockpile included 83,000 tonnes of wheat flour, 77,000 tonnes of rice and 55,000 tonnes of sugar.

Some 20,000 troops launched "Operation Jaya Sikuru" or "Sure of Victory", from Vavuniya, 40 km (25 miles) southwest of Nedunkeni, on May 13 in a bid to open a supply route to the Jaffna peninsula, 100 km (60 miles) further north.

The LTTE, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the north and east of mainly Sinhalese Sri Lanka, have accused Colombo of killing Tamil civilians and destroying crops and property under the pretext of opening a supply route, and of creating a refugee crisis that was getting out of control.
The government began transporting fresh food supplies to the rebel heartland of Wanni on Saturday after reports that stocks were running low.
Aid workers have said food stocks in the area were strained by the number of fresh refugees and because government supplies had ground to a halt after the latest military offensive.
The government says several thousand tonnes of wheat flour, rice, sugar and milk powder had been sent to the Wanni since last October.
It says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war against Tamil separatists, now in its 14th year. The LTTE says the toll is higher.
